title: Annotatio V §.I: broader vs stricter (mastication); Impropria mental — natural vs supernatural
pass_a_gloss: And it is either more broadly so called about any foodstuff properly so called; or more strictly, concerned with foodstuff solid in kind, which from the reason of the foodstuff’s solidity takes on a new and special action called Mastication, by which it is distinguished from swallowing — so essential to the eating of solider foodstuff, whether done with the teeth or the gum, that even Eating is put for Mastication as for the more famous analog, and food eaten signifies not so much food consumed as food chewed and broken by the teeth and masticated, as Calepinus witnesses. IMPROPER Eating is a mental action, consisting in the reception and use of that by which the mind is fed and perfected — i.e. in the Cognition of things and the rumination of those known things instituted by the mind. And it is either purely Mental, performed by the mind considered as to its nature through Cognition of things knowable by nature — hence to be called Mental Natural; or moreover Spiritual, occupied by a Mind illuminated and regenerated by the Holy Spirit around things knowable by the sole virtue of Illumination and Regeneration, knowing and using them — and so to be named Mental Supernatural.
pass_b_english: Proper eating is broader (any foodstuff) or stricter (solid food needing mastication — Calepinus: ‘eaten’ often means chewed).
IMPROPER eating is mental: knowing and ruminating what feeds the mind — either Mental Natural, or Mental Supernatural when the Spirit-illuminated mind knows regeneration-things.
source_text: Estque vel latiùs dicta circa quodcunque esculentum propriè dictum; vel strictiùs, circa esculentum, in specie solidum, versata, quæ ex ratione soliditatis esculenti, novam specialemque actionem adsciscit, Masticationem vocatam, quâ à deglutitione distinguitur, Manducationi solidioris esculenti adeo essentialem, sive dentibus, sive gingivâ peragatur, ut etiam Manducatio, pro Masticatione, ceu pro analogo famosiori, ponatur, cibusque manducatus, non tàm comestum, quàm mansum & dentibus comminutum masticatumque cibum significet, teste Calepino. IMPROPRIA Manducatio est actio mentalis, consistens in receptione & usurpatione ejus, quô mens alitur atque perficitur, i. e. in Cognitione rerum, harumque cognitarum ruminatione, à mente instituta. Estque vel purè Mentalis, à mente, quoad naturam suam considerata, per Cognitionem rerum, naturâ noscibilium, peracta, ob id Mentalis Naturalis dicenda; vel præterea Spiritualis, à Mente per Sp. S. illuminata ac regenerata, circa res, solâ virtute Illuminationis & Regenerationis, cognoscibiles, cognoscendo & usurpando occupata, eóque Mentalis Supernaturalis nuncupanda.
